description:
Define the core extension data structures and behaviour.

**Extension struct:**
```elixir
%Extension{
  id: String.t(),
  path: String.t(),
  handlers: %{event_type() => [handler_fn()]},
  tools: %{String.t() => Tool.t()},
  commands: %{String.t() => command()},
}
```

**Event types (26 total, from upstream types.ts lines 938-959):**

Fire-and-forget (no return needed):
- session_start, session_shutdown, agent_start, agent_end
- turn_start, turn_end, message_start, message_update, message_end
- tool_execution_start, tool_execution_update, tool_execution_end
- model_select, session_compact, after_provider_response, session_tree

Cancel-on-result (first truthy cancels):
- session_before_switch, session_before_fork
- session_before_compact, session_before_tree

Reduce-chain (handlers transform value sequentially):
- context (transforms messages list)
- before_provider_request (transforms payload)
- input (transforms text + images, or returns :handled to stop)

Mutate-in-place (handlers modify event.input):
- tool_call (can block execution or mutate args)

Patch-merge (handlers return partial patches):
- tool_result (patches content, details, is_error)

First-result-wins / collect-all:
- user_bash (first non-nil result used)
- before_agent_start (accumulate messages, chain system_prompt)
- resources_discover (collect all paths)

**Handler signature:** `(event, context) -> result | nil`

**Extension behaviour:**
```elixir
@callback init(api :: ExtensionAPI.t()) :: :ok | {:ok, state}
```

Extensions register handlers via the API during init.

**Upstream ref:** types.ts (1543 lines), runner.ts lines 673-1018
title: Extension behaviour + event types + handler storage
